_comment: TARGET-tier scope definition for a WRAP-ONLY campaign over libxml2
v2.15.3. There is no port scope: nothing is translated to native Rust.
The deliverable is a safe Rust wrapper over the whole published C API,
so the target is defined by the headers that publish it.
_comment_files: The target's file set: everything this campaign covers. One explicit
list - there is no port/wrap split here, because scope says what the
target CONTAINS, not what will be done with it. Port or wrap is the
translate stage's objective, chosen per unit by the orchestrator.
Both halves are needed and the reason is easy to get wrong: entity
classification is DEFINITION-anchored. Listing only include/libxml/
would admit just what those headers DEFINE - inline functions, macros,
the public value structs - while every function they merely DECLARE
(xmlNewDoc, xmlTextWriterStartElement, ...) has its body in a root .c
and would fall out of scope entirely. The C sources carry the bodies;
the headers carry the public value types and the declarations.
The API-surface question - wrap the public headers, not the internals -
is answered at SELECTION time (`--file include/libxml/xmlwriter.h`),
not by narrowing scope. That keeps the ownership analysis able to walk
the real implementation of everything it wraps.
`./` walks the repo root, which is where libxml2's 55 .c files live.

_comment_out_of_scope: `paths` removes what `files: ['./']` would otherwise sweep in: the test
harness, the fuzzers, the Python bindings, the examples and the
generated/vendored build scaffolding. None of it is libxml2's shipped
`features` is documentation only - no composer reads it. It lists the
LIBXML2_WITH_* options OFF in the configure line recorded in build.json,
so a body they elide contributes no entities and drops out on its own.
